title: Stop the points balance from losing promotions

blocks.text: The shop keeps each member's loyalty points in a `PointsAccount`. Purchases add points from the request threads, refunds take them away, and batch jobs run promotions ("double every balance this weekend") and expiry ("half of it expires") over every account, at the same time as the shop is busy. Support has a pile of tickets from members whose points went back to an old balance after a promotion, and the balance field is already `volatile`.

Finish `apply(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/PointsAccount.java`. A rule computes the new balance from the current one and has no side effects; some rules take a while to compute. When you're done, no rule is lost when rules arrive together, and each rule applies to the balance as it is when the rule takes effect. You may change how the balance is stored. About three lines in total.
The tests hold one rule in the middle of its computation while another thread applies a second rule, then let the first one finish.

cases.says: rules applied one after another each change the balance and return the new balance
points earned while a bonus is being computed are still in the balance after the bonus is applied
a rule that depends on the balance applies to the balance as it is when it takes effect, not as it was when it started computing
a bonus whose balance changed while it was computing is still applied, not dropped

origin.section: volatile Makes Each Read and Each Write Atomic, Never a Read Followed by a Write

concepts: Re-checking a volatile field before writing, or applying a computed difference with addAndGet, leaves a read followed by a write and loses or misapplies updates.
volatile makes each read and each write atomic but never a read followed by a write; an update computed from the current value needs an atomic class's updateAndGet or compareAndSet, or a lock.
